lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: The chronology and status of the projects are unclear because the Aug 2025–Present project may overlap other entries.
items.because: Readers should not have to infer how the projects, internship, and in-progress M.S. fit together.

items.says: Dates should use a consistent format with en dashes rather than hyphens.
The résumé should remain one page for early-career roles unless the extra project detail is essential.
The technical explanations are inconsistent in specificity and sometimes omit the contribution or evaluation setup.
items.because: Some bullets are highly specific while others lack essential context.

items.says: Some bullets use excessive jargon for a general recruiting audience.
items.because: Technical specificity should remain understandable while demonstrating expertise.

items.says: The phone number, email domain, and code URL are placeholders rather than real professional contact information.
items.because: They should be replaced with actual contact details.

items.says: The code link should point directly to a GitHub, GitLab, portfolio, or relevant project page.
items.because: A generic code path may not establish what it contains.

items.says: The header could include a current and useful LinkedIn profile.
The date of birth should be removed.
items.because: Age and date of birth are not normally relevant to hiring in the U.S. or Canada and can create bias concerns.

items.says: Nationality should be removed unless specifically requested.
items.because: Only applicable work authorization or visa status may be useful for the role.

items.says: The M.S. entry could add a relevant specialization, thesis topic, coursework, research area, or project.
items.because: It should be included only if it supports the target role.

items.says: The location format should be consistent with the other education entry.
The B.S. entry could add a strong GPA, honors, or a relevant senior project.
items.because: These may help an early-career candidate if they do not crowd out stronger experience.

items.says: The placeholder location “Country” should be replaced with the real country name.
“Diagnostic accuracy” needs a defined metric such as exact match, F1, or top-k accuracy.
The comparison point for the 35% improvement is unclear.
items.because: It should identify whether the comparison is before fine-tuning, against a baseline, or against a prior checkpoint.

items.says: “Validated tool-use trajectories” and the validation process need clarification.
items.because: The phrase is opaque to general ML recruiters.

items.says: Assistant-only loss masking needs an explanation if retained.
items.because: It should not be repeated in another bullet.

items.says: The 35% figure is ambiguous between a percentage-point increase and a relative improvement.
“In-scope signals” and the routing decision need clarification.
The method used to measure reviewer disagreement is unclear.
items.because: Disagreement could mean label mismatch, recommendation conflict, or unsupported conclusions.

items.says: The evaluation sample size or test-set scope is missing.
items.because: The change from 14% to 6% is more credible when the number of assessed cases is known.

items.says: The reviewer’s claimed independence needs clarification.
items.because: Shared prompts, tools, or model components would require a more precise description.

items.says: GRPO should be defined at first use for general software or ML recruiters.
The conditions behind “at equal accuracy” are unclear.
items.because: It should state whether accuracy was statistically equivalent, exactly matched, or merely not materially lower.

items.says: “Grouped tool-use rollouts” needs explanation for readers outside reinforcement learning.
The workload or evaluation volume behind the tool-call and latency reductions is missing.
The bullet does not show that the reward avoided trading away answer quality, citation quality, or failure recovery.
The specific contribution to the evaluation harness is unclear.
items.because: It could have involved test design, data pipelines, metrics, dashboards, CI integration, or release gating.

items.says: “Citation quality” is not defined.
How the harness caught the two regressions is unclear.
items.because: It may have blocked releases, flagged review, or identified them retrospectively.

items.says: The test-set size or evaluation frequency is missing.
items.because: Fourteen checkpoints shows breadth but not the scale of each evaluation.

items.says: This bullet duplicates the assistant-only loss-masking work already described in line 9.
items.because: The technique should remain only in the bullet containing the measurable accuracy result.

items.says: The claim about reproducing tool outputs describes intent rather than demonstrated impact.
items.because: It lacks a supporting metric for a standalone result.

items.says: The 800-signal triage and backlog result duplicates the Research-Agent project bullet.
items.because: The same accomplishment should not appear in both sections.

items.says: It is unclear which position or project owns the triage work.
items.because: The result appears under both the internship and the Research-Agent project.

items.says: “Branch” needs to be defined as a workflow branch, model route, product feature, or deployment path.
The measurement and causality of the 68% backlog reduction need clarification.
items.because: Other operational changes may also have contributed.

items.says: The comparison window for the eight-week result is unclear.
The type of GPU memory represented by the 4x reduction is unclear.
items.because: It could mean peak allocated, reserved, or total job memory.

items.says: The bullet does not state whether quality, throughput, batch size, and convergence remained comparable.
items.because: Changing precision can affect those areas.

items.says: “Perception models” is too broad and could identify the model type or workload.
The environment used to measure 420 ms and 180 ms is unclear.
items.because: The figures could come from production, load testing, or staging.

items.says: It is unclear whether the 200 ms build threshold is a hard release gate.
The cache’s freshness or correctness constraints are not explained.
The separate contributions of caching and batching are not distinguished.
The verbs have inconsistent tense: “maintained” is past tense while “adds” is present tense.
It is unclear whether the candidate added the regression checks or only maintained checks created by someone else.
“Release cycles to 3 days” is ambiguous.
items.because: It could mean deployment frequency, code-freeze-to-release time, or validation duration.

items.says: The conditions covered by the regression checks are unspecified.
items.because: They could cover accuracy, latency, memory, compatibility, or other criteria.

items.says: The candidate’s role in the migration is unclear.
items.because: It could include owning the migration, designing the schema, implementing consumers, or coordinating rollout.

items.says: The former nightly backlog lacks volume or delay figures.
items.because: Those figures would make the operational result stronger.

items.says: The bullet lacks a quantified reliability result.
items.because: It could report retry recovery, fewer failed jobs, or improved dispatch availability.

items.says: The handling of failed dead-letter events needs explanation for a broader audience.
The visible line break in “dead-letter” should be avoided.
items.because: Wrapping should come from document layout rather than manual line breaks.

items.says: “Owner” is vague.
items.because: It should specify sole developer, technical lead, maintainer, or project owner.

items.says: The project is not identified as personal, academic, open-source, or employer-related.
“Present” should be verified as accurate when the résumé is submitted.
The bullet is broad and promotional and does not identify what was built or changed.
The “AI-first engineering practices” and affected teams are not identified.
“Accelerating delivery” and “improving outcomes” are unsupported by specific metrics.
items.because: Without evidence, they read as unsupported claims.

items.says: “Working context” and how it was measured need clarification.
The baseline and final sizes behind “raw conversation grew 100x” are unclear.
items.because: They should be understandable and technically consistent.

items.says: The quality or reliability tradeoff from staged compaction is not reported.
items.because: The bullet should show whether task success, tool-call correctness, or evaluation performance was preserved.

items.says: The stress-test success criteria and number of runs are missing.
The separate concurrency pools are not identified.
The bullet does not explain why separating the pools prevented deadlocks.
“50-way fan-out” is not defined as concurrent agents, tool calls, or tasks.
“Removing” deadlocks and lost results may overstate the evidence without before-and-after failure rates or extensive testing.
It is unclear whether the issue occurred in production, a reproducible stress test, or only as a design risk.
The contribution to the eight metrics is unclear.
items.because: It should distinguish implementing metrics from integrating libraries or building adapters and reporting.

items.says: The open-source framework is not identified or linked.
The meaning of “8 metrics” is ambiguous.
items.because: It could refer to distinct evaluators, variants, or evaluation dimensions.

items.says: The bullet omits test coverage, runtime impact, or adoption.
items.because: Those details should be included if meaningful.

items.says: “Injected degradation” and how the reports were altered need definition.
What the Kendall correlation measured is unclear.
The statistical significance of the 0.89 correlation is not reported.
The unit of the 400-plus report-level trials is unclear.
items.because: They could be distinct reports, repeated perturbations, or model-generated reports.

items.says: This backlog result duplicates the Mobility Systems internship triage work.
items.because: Repeating the same accomplishment can look like padding or duplicate credit.

items.says: If this is separate work, the dataset, product, timeframe, and result are not distinguished from the internship version.
Git is incorrectly grouped with programming languages.
items.because: Git is a tool, not a programming language.

items.says: The skills list may omit relevant serving, testing, CI, queue, cloud, and model-training tools used in the experience section.
items.because: The listed skills should reflect technologies genuinely used in the work.

items.says: Capitalization and terminology should be standardized.
The implementation libraries or platforms used for these techniques are missing.
“Agent evaluation” is a capability area rather than a specific technology.
items.because: It should be supported by the bullets or replaced with concrete frameworks and methods.

items.says: The skills section omits mixed precision, caching, event queues, CI, and concurrency despite their prominence in the experience bullets.
items.because: The skills section should align with the target roles and demonstrated work.
